newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Valero sees gas unit deal by May.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Valero sees gas unit deal by May.

text.p: Valero Energy Corp chairman and chief executive officer Bill Greehey said on Thursday that the company could deal away its natural gas services unit by May if all goes according to schedule.
He said offering brochures would be sent shortly to 37 companies thought to have an interest in the unit, which he said was valued at "$1.4 billion plus."
"By February we hope that we've selected someone. If they don't require an IRS tax ruling, we'd have a shareholders meeting in may and it could be done in May," Greehey told Reuters in an interview.
Greehey said Valero wanted to wrap up a deal soon because "there is a strong feeling (the government) will make these kinds of transactions taxable (in 1998)."
He said, too, that Valero was moving quickly because there is an natural gas industry trend toward consolidation.

"There are so many mergers, we felt like if you don't get out there pretty quick, the right merger partner is not going to be there because they've already found someone else," he said. Of the 37 companies Valero believes most likely to be interested in a deal, 16 are electric utilities, Greehey said.

"I think you're going to see more and more of those mergers (between natural gas firm and utilities)," he said. "They're (utilities) looking for the culture of a non- regulated company and someone that can manage their fuel costs -- and the largest market for natural gas is electricity generation."
Greehey said Valero had had one-on-one talks with many companies about the natural gas unit, but finally decided that "to get the best price, it would have to be on a bid basis."
Valero has a 7,500-mile pipeline system with a throughput capacity of 3 billion cubic feet of gas a day.

Greehey said Valero felt that, with changes now taking place in the natural gas business, it was not large enough by itself to survive. "If we ran business as usual, we'd get pretty well squeezed out," he said.
Greehey said a transaction would be "stock for stock. They'd be acquiring all the Valero stock and in turn would give Valero shareholders some of their stock."

Valero's refining and marketing arm would be spun off into a separate company -- still with the Valero name -- with $1.6 billion assets and $900 million in equity, Greehey said. Its primary asset would be a refinery in Corpus Christi, Texas.
"It would give us the ability to really grow that business, which we haven't had because of the heavy debt we've had in our company. We're about 49 percent debt," he said.
Greehey said Valero's 4th quarter performance was "looking really good. We've been long on gas, so as these gas prices have just gone out of sight we've made a lot of money.

"And (gas) liquids prices are just very, very good. Refining margins are strong and resid discounts good, so the 4th quarter looks a whole lot better than it did two months ago," he said. Valero earned $0.23 a share in the 3rd quarter, down $0.45 in the same period a year ago.
